rationale: A better helps a careful decision-maker because it distinguishes seed distribution from viral amplification, directly compares all live alternatives, and gives conditional guidance: choose partnerships unless performance is currently bad, treat mobile/load as hygiene thresholds, and start partnership work early due to lead-time risk. B is clear and plausible, but it assumes initial exposure can be handled separately and dismisses partnerships as not really a feature, which may not fit the scenario. Neither is strongly quantitative, but A at least uses threshold-style numbers and more explicit caveats.
